profile.campus: Silicon Valley (San Jose, Santa Clara County, CA) -- likely STACK's SVY01 campus area, not SVY02
profile.reading: This building is one of two adjacent structures that OpenStreetMap contributors have separately mapped and tagged as Stack Infrastructure buildings in San Jose, California, within Santa Clara County, and it is the westernmost of the pair. Comparing the two records' underlying map geometry confirms they are genuinely separate buildings rather than duplicate points for a single structure: this one has a simple rectangular footprint roughly 155 by 60 meters with a mapped roof height of about 8.5 meters, while its companion building about 70 meters to the east has a more irregular, multi wing footprint and a lower mapped height of about 5.6 meters. Both sit in the Fortune Drive and Trade Zone Boulevard corridor of San Jose, which is the same immediate area where STACK Infrastructure's own site places its SVY01 campus, a 100 megawatt, four building, 19 acre data center campus, rather than the company's separately documented SVY02 campus in Santa Clara, a single 560,440 square foot former Memorex headquarters building rated at 48 megawatts of IT capacity that an earlier pass through this database had linked to these two San Jose buildings. The same immediate neighborhood is also the site of a newer STACK expansion that the City of San Jose's planning department reviewed under the name Trade Zone Park, a 9.8 acre project at 2400 Ringwood Avenue and 1849 Fortune Drive comprising two four story data center buildings totaling about 522,000 square feet, plus an advanced manufacturing building and a 91 megawatt backup generating facility, which cleared City Council review in May 2023. Because the two buildings mapped here are lower rise than the four story buildings described in that 2023 filing, they more plausibly correspond to two of SVY01's four existing buildings than to the newer Trade Zone Park buildings, though public sources do not allow a building by building match with certainty. STACK Infrastructure, headquartered in Denver, Colorado, is a global data center developer and operator with more than 8.5 gigawatts of capacity built or under development across 24 markets in the Americas, Asia Pacific, and EMEA. Santa Clara County, which includes both San Jose and Santa Clara, is broadly recognized within the industry as one of the most land, power, and water constrained data center markets in the country, which is part of why STACK's own materials describe Silicon Valley vacancy running consistently below the national average even as the company continues to add capacity there.

profile.research_note: CORRECTION to earlier pass: coordinates (37.4025598,-121.893391) and companion way 553223629 (37.4022094,-121.8923868) both reverse-geocode into San Jose 95131 (Fortune Drive / Trade Zone Blvd corridor), NOT Santa Clara. STACK's SVY02 (48MW, single 560,440sqft building, former Memorex HQ) is in Santa Clara city, a different city from San Jose within the same county, so the earlier identification of these two ways as SVY02 (via a website field pointing to the svy02 URL) appears to be wrong. Official OSM way records (fetched via api.openstreetmap.org) show way 553223628 is a simple 9-node rectangle, height 8.46m, and way 553223629 is a complex 21-node footprint, height 5.58m, bbox approx 233x62m -- genuinely different buildings, not a duplicate pair. City of San Jose planning records document a separate, newer 'STACK Trade Zone Park' EIR project (SCH 2022060141) at 2400 Ringwood Ave / 1849 Fortune Dr: 9.8 acres, two 4-story DC buildings (~522,194 sqft combined), 91MW backup generator capacity, approved May 2023. Because our two OSM ways were mapped Dec 2022 (before that May 2023 approval) and are lower-rise than 4 stories, they more plausibly represent 2 of the 4 existing SVY01 buildings (100MW/19 acres/4 buildings per stackinfra.com) than the newer Trade Zone Park buildings. Could not confirm which of SVY01's lettered buildings (01A-D, 9-36MW each) each way corresponds to. Prior building_sqft=560440 and it_capacity_mw=48 values (attributed to SVY02) are now considered unconfirmed for this specific building and cleared.
profile.sources_tried: Nominatim reverse geocode at stored coordinates (37.4025598,-121.893391) returns "Microsoft Corporation, 2001 Fortune Drive, San Jose, CA 95131" as the named building, not a Stack Infrastructure-tagged building (unlike the adjacent Stack rows at 2130 Trade Zone Blvd and 2150 Trade Zone Blvd, which resolve cleanly). Possibly a Stack-built facility now occupied/branded by Microsoft, or a stale coordinate. Needs Santa Clara County parcel check to confirm current occupant/owner.

reading.body:
This facility is one of four buildings on Stack Infrastructure's San Jose campus, SVY01, which the operator publishes at 100 MW total across 1,030,000 square feet of data hall space on 19 acres. The specific building represented by this registry row cannot be determined from the operator's published pages; it is most plausibly one of four structures ranging from 140,000 to 350,000 square feet each. No individual building capacity is published.

Stack Infrastructure has not published a cooling or IT load specification for this facility. If IT load runs at 40 kW per rack, a common density for AI training clusters, the campus's 100 MW would support roughly 2,500 racks; the actual density at this site is not disclosed. No certifications or compliance specifications are published for this campus.

This campus sits in California, which has 103 mapped data center facilities and 365 MW of published capacity across 11 facilities. The SVY01 campus ranks twelfth among California facilities for published capacity. Stack Infrastructure operates three separate campuses in Silicon Valley totaling 150 MW; this row covers one of them and cannot be individually ranked against other state facilities.
